title: Scenario-driven roadmap & OKR mapping for Private/VPC/onprem Q2
creator: Elena Park
description: Objective: produce a scenario-driven quarterly roadmap that ties discrete Private/VPC/on‑prem feature deliverables to measurable OKRs and failure budgets. This ticket coordinates cross-functional inputs (serving runtime, infra, security, solutions) to create three prioritized scenarios (Conservative: SLA-first; Balanced: cost+SLA; Aggressive: high-automation onramp) and convert them into an actionable sprint plan and acceptance gates for Q2. Scope: definition of scenarios and decision criteria, assignment of sprint-level milestones, identification of must-have compatibility tests, upgrade/migration windows, and a customer cohort staging plan. Out-of-scope: implementation work for specific infra tasks (split into ENG tickets), deep security design (handled by Security review ticket). Key deliverables: scenario matrix, OKR map (with owners and signals), risk-adjusted sequencing with rollback criteria, stakeholder commitment slate, runbook links and smoke-test checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Scenario matrix with explicit trade-offs (latency, cost, engineering effort) created and reviewed by Eng/Research
OKR mapping: for each scenario list 3 measurable signals and owners (latency P95, unit cost per 1M tokens, onboarding time)
Sprint plan: milestone-level breakdown for Q2 with dependency owners and dates
Compatibility gate list: matrix of customer/OS/hypervisor combos with test owners
Runbook & rollback criteria documented and linked; exec sign-off obtained from Product, Infra, and Security
comments: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting — aligned on three scenarios. Action: Eng to produce estimated effort per scenario (ENG-2245).

2026-03-02: Security requested encrypted artifact transport requirement; added as must-have for Conservative and Balanced scenarios. (see security note: https://confluence.redwood.com/security/private-onprem-transport)
2026-03-05: PM review with Sales — identified 4 enterprise customers for early cohort; added onboarding windows and SLA expectations to matrix.
2026-03-08: Design reviewed initial onboarding UX flows for on‑prem agent; feedback captured in https://drive.redwood.com/design/private-onprem-agent-v1
2026-03-10: Roadmap draft circulated for exec read; requested clearer failure-budget mapping to OKRs (action: update by 2026-03-14).

Artifacts: Confluence plan https://confluence.redwood.com/PM/PM-438888-scenario-roadmap, Draft slides https://drive.redwood.com/slides/PM-438888-q2-plan, Perf dashboard snapshot https://grafana.redwood.com/d/pm438888/q2-scenario-sim
notes: Trade-offs discussed: delaying aggressive automation reduces short-term onramp but lowers regression risk for high-security tenants.
Recommended default: Balanced scenario as baseline for Q2 to hit OKR targets while preserving headroom for dedicated customers.
Next steps: finalize metric thresholds for OKRs (latency P95 threshold, onboarding time <= 5 days for cohort A) and convert to measurable dashboard tiles.
